findings.title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem inside rules.map()
findings.body: In `FilterViewResults`, the `grafana` branch of `rules.map(...)` now renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, while the `datasource` and `default` branches still pass `key={key}`. The pre-computed `key` (from `getRuleKey`) is destructured but unused for Grafana rules. This produces a React "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warning and makes reconciliation index-based; because this list grows by appending pages during infinite scroll, items can be re-created/re-ordered incorrectly and transient component state (e.g. an open action menu or drawer) can be attached to the wrong row.

findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view
findings.body: `AlertRuleMenu` now computes Grafana abilities from `promRule` (so Pause/Delete can be "allowed" without a ruler rule), but the rendering conditions were not updated: the Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). In the new rule list (`GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` with only `promRule`), `rulerRule` is always undefined, so users can no longer pause or delete a rule from the list view even when they have permission. Note the delete handler itself only needs the identifier (`showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), so the gate is unnecessary. The new assertion `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx bakes this regression into the tests, and the `ui.menuItems.delete` selector added there is never used.

findings.title: "Silence notifications" menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is available
findings.body: The silence drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, where `rule` is the ruler rule. In the new list view only `promRule` is passed, so `rule` is undefined and `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is never mounted. Meanwhile `AlertRuleMenu` now derives the Silence ability from the Prometheus rule (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), so the "Silence notifications" item is shown (the new GrafanaGroupLoader test even asserts it exists). Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true and nothing happens — a visible, clickable action with no effect and no feedback.

findings.title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause/Export/Restore abilities in the Prometheus ability path
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the gate for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` (lines 324-330). The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes Grafana recording rules. Since Grafana-managed recording rules can be paused and exported, routing the list view through this hook silently removes the Pause, Export, Restore and Delete-permanently actions for every Grafana recording rule. Only `Silence` legitimately requires an alerting rule.

findings.title: skipToken path grants Duplicate ability for non-Grafana rules
findings.body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken, ...)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which does not short-circuit: with `rule === undefined`, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported`, `isPluginProvided` is false so `duplicateSupported = true`, and `Duplicate` becomes `[true, ctx.hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]`. `AlertRuleMenu` ORs this with the ruler ability (`canDuplicate = ruler || grafana`), so for data-source (Mimir/Loki/Prometheus) rules — which always pass `skipToken` — the "Duplicate" item is shown to any user holding the Grafana `alert.rules:create` permission, even when the data source has no ruler or the user lacks external-write permission. The hook should return an all-false ability map when no rule is supplied.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable in the existing rule views
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the `CombinedRule`, which disabled Update/Delete/Pause for Mimir federated rule groups. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` (the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was dropped). As a result, every consumer of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (RulesTable, rule details, etc.) will now offer Edit/Delete on federated rules, which the backend rejects. The group information is no longer plumbed into the hook, so this needs an explicit fix (or at least the group's `source_tenants` passed through) rather than a TODO.

findings.title: Provisioned-rule protection in the new list view is untested and depends on a newly declared optional field
findings.body: `provenance?: string` is added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and `isProvisionedPromRule` / `GrafanaRuleListItem` (`isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)`) now rely exclusively on it to mark Grafana rules as provisioned in the ruler-less list view. No mock, fixture or test sets `provenance` on a Prometheus rule (e.g. `rulerRuleToPromRule` in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx omits it), and no test asserts that a provisioned rule hides Edit/Delete through this path. If the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not return `provenance`, provisioned rules will silently become editable/deletable in the list, so this behaviour needs a test that pins it down.

findings.title: Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The replacement omits `returnTo`, so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page no longer provides the "return to previous" target and the user loses the back-navigation affordance to their filtered list.

findings.title: logWarning is emitted during render for every affected row
findings.body: `getEditableIdentifier` is called directly in the component body and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` whenever neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana Prometheus rule is supplied. Because this runs on every render — and the rule list polls Prometheus every 20s, re-rendering all rows — a single unsupported row will emit the same warning repeatedly, spamming the analytics backend. Move the reporting into an effect (or dedupe it) so it fires once per occurrence.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name after removing ruler prefetching
findings.body: The ruler prefetch (`alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)`) was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules ... but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers into thinking ruler data is still warmed up here.
